content.text: Find the best Keplerian fit for hypothesis H2 (two planets, starting periods 111.3 d and 32.0 d; the 111 d exceeds the 106.7 d baseline, so let it range longer). Report fit ID, periods, amplitudes, eccentricities, RMS vs 1.58 m/s limit, BIC, and residual periodogram peaks (flag any with false-alarm probability below 1e-3). Be fast — under 3 minutes.

content.text:
H2 explains the data: a two-planet fit gets the scatter under the limit, beats the one-planet fit by a wide margin on BIC, and leaves no significant signal in the residuals.

**Best fit: F3** (hypothesis H2, periods allowed to move ±50% from their starting values)

| Planet | Period | Semi-amplitude K | Eccentricity |
|---|---|---|---|
| b | 116.57 d | 29.28 m/s | 0.251 |
| c | 31.14 d | 13.97 m/s | 0.020 |

- **Scatter (RMS):** 1.13 m/s, limit 1.58 m/s, so it passes. Reduced χ² is 1.34, where 1 would mean a perfect match to the measurement errors.
- **BIC:** 278.8, lower is better. The best one-planet fit (F2, H1) has a BIC of 5927.6, so H2 is lower by about 5649. The plan's bar was an improvement of at least 10.
- **Flags:**
  - No period is stuck on a search bound, so the wider range was enough.
  - Planet b's 116.6 d period is longer than the 106.7 d observing baseline, so it is poorly constrained.
- **Residual periodogram:** the strongest leftover peak is at 1.274 d with false-alarm probability 0.022, above the 1e-3 threshold. All other peaks (1.62, 3.50, 1.56, 1.14 and 1.34 d) have false-alarm probabilities of 0.29 or higher. No peak falls below 1e-3, so nothing points to a third planet.

H2's two planets fully account for the data. The main open question is planet b's exact period, and data covering more than about 220 days would pin it down.
